findings.issue: build-code facts.review is only checked for artifact_path/artifact_paths when it is an object. The generic required-key check treats any non-empty scalar as valid, so a stage-result with facts.review:"pass" currently passes validateStageResult without any raw JSON review artifact. I reproduced this locally with validateStageResult("build-code", artifact) returning ok:true for review:"pass".
findings.recommendation: Require facts.review to be an object for build-code before accepting it, then require artifact_path or artifact_paths to contain at least one non-empty .json path. Add a negative test for facts.review as a string/array/number.

findings.issue: The updated workflow says buildReviewFact enforces the facts.review schema and now documents raw JSON verdict paths, but the actual producer helper still accepts any non-empty artifactPath and existing tests still assert review.md/x.md are valid. That keeps the producer contract inconsistent with the new gate/stage facts contract: build-code can still construct Markdown review facts that later fail validation.
findings.recommendation: Update workflows/build-code/facts-schema.mjs and its tests so executed review facts require a raw JSON artifact path, or change this SKILL.md line to stop claiming the helper enforces that contract and add an explicit validation step before stage-result assembly. Recommended: enforce .json in buildReviewFact and update tests/build-code-review.test.mjs away from .md positives.

resolutionSummary: revise_required: targeted tests and git diff --check pass, but build-code review fact validation still has a false-pass scalar path, and the documented raw JSON producer contract is not enforced by buildReviewFact.

findings.description: Spec describes or requires eliminating internal contradictions between field contracts or rule statements (cluster A: schema/contract terms + cluster B: conflict/contradiction/duplicate terms). Multiple conflicting schemas for the same entity cause silent drift — schema-drift blocking.
